Advanced Last verified: 2026-07-17. Headless flags and CI integration details evolve — confirm against the official Claude Code / Agent SDK docs. Confirm against the official source. A classic high-value automation: have Claude review every pull request and post its findings as a comment — running headless in CI. Here's the shape, with the guardrails that keep it safe.
documents.s: GitHub Action that Reviews Every PR

documents.t: On each PR: check out the diff, ask Claude to review it for bugs/edge-cases/convention issues, and post a comment. Humans still decide; Claude just gives a fast first pass.

name: Claude PR review on: pull_request permissions: contents: read pull-requests: write # to comment — NOT write to code jobs: review: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4 with: { fetch-depth: 0 } - name: Review the diff env: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }} run: | git diff origin/${{ github.base_ref }}...HEAD > /tmp/diff.patch claude -p "Review this diff for correctness bugs, missing edge cases, and security issues. Report ONLY high-confidence findings as a Markdown checklist with file:line. Diff:" < /tmp/diff.patch > /tmp/review.md # then post /tmp/review.md as a PR comment (e.g. with the gh CLI or an action) (Exact headless invocation may differ — see the docs. The principle is: feed the diff, capture Markdown, post it.)

:::warning Least privilege in CI Comment only. Grant pull-requests: write, not contents: write — the bot shouldn't push code. Scope the token; never expose deploy/secret access to a job that reads untrusted PR content. Treat PR content as untrusted — it can carry prompt injection; don't let the job take consequential actions. Cap cost — large diffs cost tokens; consider reviewing changed files only. :::
Ask for high-confidence findings only — a wall of nitpicks gets ignored. Keep it as a first pass, with humans making the merge call.

Intermediate Last verified: 2026-09-21. Deprecation schedules and migration details come from Anthropic and change — always confirm dates and replacements in the official docs before migrating. Confirm against the official source. Models get retired, parameters get renamed, behaviors shift. This page tracks breaking changes so upgrades don't surprise you. If you build on the API, skim it periodically.
A pinned model ID will eventually be deprecated and then removed. Code that hard-codes it breaks. A little hygiene prevents 2am surprises.

Read model IDs from config, never scatter literals across the codebase — then migrating is a one-line change. Watch announcements for deprecation dates and recommended replacements. Re-run your evals when you switch models — behavior can shift even on a "newer, better" model. Test before the deadline, not after removal.

Change Example What to do Model retired An older model ID stops working Move to the recommended successor; re-eval Parameter superseded A reasoning/budget knob replaced by effort Update calls; see Thinking & Effort Default shift A new default model/behavior Pin intentionally; verify your prompts still work Endpoint/SDK update New SDK major version Read the migration guide; bump deliberately
The authoritative schedule lives on the official model deprecations page — confirm dates there before you migrate. Anthropic gives at least 60 days' notice before retiring a publicly released model.

No publicly released Claude model is currently in the "deprecated, not yet retired" window (checked September 21, 2026). The only deprecated ID is the invitation-only claude-mythos-preview (deprecated June 9, 2026, retirement date to be announced) — Project Glasswing participants should move to claude-mythos-5. Two earliest-possible retirement dates are now close: claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929 (not sooner than September 29, 2026) and claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 (not sooner than October 15, 2026). Neither has been deprecated, and any retirement still requires at least 60 days' notice — but if you pin either ID, plan the migration now. Confirm against the official model status table.

claude-opus-4-1-20250805 (Opus 4.1) was retired August 5, 2026 — move to claude-opus-4-8 (or straight to claude-opus-5). claude-opus-4-20250514 (Opus 4) and claude-sonnet-4-20250514 (Sonnet 4) were retired June 15, 2026 — Anthropic's listed replacements are claude-opus-4-8 and claude-sonnet-4-6 respectively (or go straight to claude-opus-5 / claude-sonnet-5). Calls to any retired ID now return an API error. If your code still pins one of these, that's the first thing to fix.

On Claude Opus 4.7 and later (including Opus 4.8 and Opus 5) and on Claude Sonnet 5, the sampling knobs temperature, top_p, and top_k are deprecated: setting any of them to a non-default value returns a 400 error. Omit them and steer behavior with prompting and Thinking & Effort instead. Note that the Python SDK (v1.0 and later) removes these three parameters entirely, so passing them raises a TypeError before any request is sent; most other SDKs keep them in their request types and let the API return the 400. Always confirm your model IDs against the Current Models & Pricing table; if you're on an older ID, plan a migration.

A plain-English digest of what's changed recently across Claude — so you can skim "what's new and what it means for me" without reading every changelog. Newest first. :::info How this page stays current Entries are added by the community and by an automated watcher that flags upstream changes for a human to write up. Each entry links its official source. See something missing? Add it. :::
Each update is tagged by surface — 🗣️ Apps (chat/voice/mobile), 🛠️ Claude Code, 🔌 API, 🧠 Models — and answers "what it means for you."

🧠 Models — Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5) shipped September 22, 2026 at $4 / $20 per MTok — 20% under Opus 5, with cache reads at $0.20 / MTok (a 5% tier, not the usual 10%). Same 1M context and 128K max output, adaptive thinking always on, and the default effort drops from high to medium. Anthropic positions it at Claude Fable 5.1-level performance on most work while costing 40% less to run than Opus 5. Four breaking changes return 400 on an Opus 5 codebase: thinking can no longer be disabled, forced tool_choice is gone, thinking blocks are bound to the model and conversation that produced them, and computer_20251124 is rejected on the Claude API and Google Cloud. A fifth returns 200 and breaks nothing loudly: text between tool calls now comes back inside thinking blocks whose text is empty at the default display setting — so a UI that streams those as progress updates goes silent mid-task. What it means: this is a cheaper, faster Opus, but it is not a drop-in ID swap. Work the response-shape change first (it fails silently), then the four 400s. Full migration walkthrough with before/after code: Claude Opus 5.5: The Field Guide. Last verified: 2026-09-23. Model ID claude-opus-5-5; 1M context; 128K max output; $4 / $20 per MTok; 5m cache write $5, 1h cache write $8, cache read $0.20; default effort medium; adaptive thinking always on; Jun 2026 reliable knowledge cutoff; released September 22, 2026, retirement not sooner than September 22, 2027. Also on Amazon Bedrock (anthropic.claude-opus-5-5), Google Cloud, Microsoft Foundry, and Claude Platform on AWS. Up to 300k output tokens on the Message Batches API with the output-300k-2026-03-24 beta header. Breaking changes enumerated in What's new in Claude Opus 5.5. Confirm against the official source. 🛠️ Claude Code — Projects were rebuilt as an orchestration layer on September 17, 2026, in beta. A Project is no longer a folder of files and chats: it is now "threads that do the work and a coordinator that directs them." You brief the coordinator in the main project chat with an outcome; it scopes the request, delegates across parallel threads, reviews the outputs, and assembles the result. The key detail is what a thread actually is — a full Claude Code cloud session working on its own branch and copy of the repo, with its own context window, able to open pull requests, run tests, and spawn its own subagents, loops, and workflows. All threads share one memory pool and contribute to a library of files and artifacts. What it means: two consequences follow directly. Usage limits arrive faster, because N threads is roughly N concurrent sessions rather than one session split N ways — and thread model/effort is set separately from the coordinator's, which makes it the cost lever that matters. And the launch eligibility rule is counter-intuitive: beta went to select Pro and Max subscribers who use cloud sessions and have no existing projects on web or desktop, so long-time Projects users were the least likely to see it first. Threads are cloud-only for now. Architecture, the four-way comparison against subagents, worktrees and inter-session messaging, and the cost model: Projects: The Coordinator & Parallel Threads. Last verified: 2026-09-23. Announcement of September 17, 2026. Coordinator/thread wording, "each thread is a Claude Code cloud session working on its own branch and copy of the repo", shared memory and library, separate model/effort for coordinator chat and worker threads, "Projects can reach usage limits faster", beta eligibility (select Pro/Max cloud-session users with no existing web or desktop projects, waitlist otherwise), and "threads run in the cloud today" with local execution stated as coming. No Claude Code reference page for Projects had shipped as of this writing. Confirm against the official source. 🧠 Models (cross-AI) — DeepSeek shipped V4.1-Flash on September 10, 2026, API and MIT-licensed weights the same day. Served as deepseek-flash: a 552B MoE on a new "Causal Encoder-Decoder" architecture with Compressed Sparse Attention 2, 8B active parameters at prefill / 16B at decode, native vision, a 1M-token context, 384K max output, and a KV cache of 890 bytes per token (about a quarter of V4-Flash's HBM footprint, an eighth of its SSD storage, 72-hour global cache lifetime). Reasoning is a 1–100 integer dial: DeepSeek's own DeepSWE v1.1 ablation goes from 66.0% at effort 25 to 74.2% at 100 for ~2.5× the output tokens, and every launch benchmark was run at 100. That 74.2 sits a fifth of a point above Claude Opus 5 (74.0); Terminal-Bench 4.0 is 31.2 vs Opus 5's 51.8. Pricing per 1M tokens, peak (01:00–04:00 and 06:00–10:00 UTC weekdays): cache hit $0.006, cache miss $0.30, output $1.20; off-peak exactly half. Two silent routing changes: deepseek-v4-flash and deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp route to V4.1-Flash from September 10, and every deepseek-v4-pro call routes to V4.1-Flash at Flash rates from 04:00 UTC September 14 until V4.1-Pro launches. What it means: repository-shaped coding work (read a lot, edit a little) is now at Opus parity for an order of magnitude less; many-short-turn terminal agents are not. If you pinned Pro, your model changed on Sunday, so re-run evals. DeepSeek itself flags long-context sparse retrieval as not fully characterized. Full field guide with the six-cell price table, serving stacks, and the effort-dial protocol: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. Last verified: 2026-09-15. Model ID, routing dates, and rates from DeepSeek's announcement and pricing page; architecture, license, and effort range from the Hugging Face model card. Opus 5 / GPT-5.6 Sol comparisons are DeepSeek's launch table as reported by VentureBeat; vendor-run until independently reproduced. Confirm against the official source. 🧠 Models (cross-AI) — Google shipped Gemini 3.8 Flash on September 2, 2026, twenty days after 3.7 Flash — the third Flash in six weeks. Model ID gemini-3.8-flash, same 1M context and 64K output, thinking_level low / medium (default) / high, and the same $0.75 / $3.75 per MTok introductory price through December 31, 2026 ($1.50 / $7.50 from January 1, 2027). Google's table: DeepSWE v1.1 73.7 (up 8.4 from 65.3; Claude Opus 5 74.0), Terminal-bench 2.1 89.4 (Opus 5 89.1), HLE-Verified 54.9, and a lead over every column including Opus 5 on the finance, legal, and biology agent benchmarks; but Terminal-bench 4.0 is 19.1 vs Opus 5's 51.8 and OSWorld-2.0 59.0 vs 75.4. The catch Google states in its own words: the model "works harder," executing extra reasoning steps and calling tools iteratively, which independent reads put at ~30% more output tokens per task and ~40% more cost per task than 3.7 Flash at the identical sticker. Knowledge cutoff March 2026, but some domains limited to January 2025. A Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber variant (CWE-Bench 47.2% pass@1, 2.6× more correct Chrome patches than the best commercial models) replaces 3.5 Flash Cyber and is application-only through the new Fairwind Program. What it means: a Sonnet-priced model now at Opus parity on repository-scale bug fixing and ahead on domain agents; interactive terminal and computer-use work stays on Claude. Budget on task cost, not token price, and start thinking_level at low. Migration list, full comparison table, and the Claude-port gotchas that have not changed since 3.6: Gemini 3.8 Flash for Claude users. Last verified: 2026-09-15. Date, pricing, "works harder" language, and Cyber figures from Google's launch post; model ID and thinking_level from Google AI for Developers; cutoff and deltas from the DeepMind model card. Comparison columns are Google's evaluation report as reproduced by Vellum; token-per-task figure from Emergent's analysis of the same report. Confirm against the official source. 🛠️ Claude Code — v2.1.271 (September 14) closed a run of context-budget knobs, and this site now has the audit page to go with them. New in 2.1.271: omitClaudeMd in subagent frontmatter and --agents JSON launches a subagent without the user, project, and local CLAUDE.md files (managed policy files still load); per-command allowed_domains on Bash, PowerShell, and Monitor in auto mode with sandboxing; --accept-command <sha256> on claude plugin install / update to pin a plugin's install command; modelPricing now accepts a multiplier above 1 (up to 10) for contracted markups; fast mode in Claude Code Remote sessions; Monitor watches always get a deadline (at most 30 minutes); and /ultrareview --post posts the PR comment as soon as findings arrive. Earlier in the fortnight: bashOutputMaxChars and taskOutputMaxChars (2.1.261) cap what a command or background task returns inline (defaults ~30,000 and 32,000 characters, range 4,000–128,000), --append-subagent-system-prompt-file (2.1.261), maxEffortLevel (2.1.267), and /skill-doctor (2.1.252). What it means: the six places Claude Code spends context before you type — skill listing (capped at 1% of the window), CLAUDE.md, auto memory, subagent descriptions (15,000-token warning), tool output, and the compaction re-attach budget (25,000 tokens) — each now have a documented setting. Run the checklist once per project: Context budget audit. Last verified: 2026-09-15. Changelog entries for 2.1.261–2.1.271. Setting definitions from the settings reference; omitClaudeMd from the subagents docs; listing budget and re-attach numbers from the skills docs. Confirm against the official source. 🧠 Models — Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1) and Claude Mythos 5.1 (claude-mythos-5-1) shipped September 1, 2026. Same Mythos-class tier above Opus, same 1M context, 128K output, $10 / $50 per MTok, same tokenizer and always-on adaptive thinking as Fable 5, but cache reads dropped from $1.00 to $0.25 per MTok (0.025× base input instead of 0.1×), which is where Anthropic's "about 25% cheaper on typical workloads, up to 45% on highly agentic ones" comes from. Three changes are breaking: tool_choice of type any or tool now returns 400 (keep auto, set strict: true, and name the tool in the prompt); thinking blocks are readable only by Fable 5.1 or newer, so routing a conversation down to Opus 5 silently drops the reasoning unless you send the thinking-binding-controls-2026-08-01 header; and editing anything before a thinking block (system prompt, tools, earlier turns) invalidates later blocks, enforced as a 400 for accounts created on or after August 31, 2026. Five are additive, all beta: per-message effort without a cache miss (mid-conversation-output-config-2026-07-01), turn-scoped system messages via clear_at: "next_user_message" (mid-conversation-system-clear-at-2026-08-21), thinking.display: "updates" to surface progress notes between tool calls (thinking-display-updates-2026-08-18), the cheaper cache read, and a statistical text watermark plus C2PA credentials on generated files. Anthropic's positioning is unchanged: start with Opus 5; use Fable 5.1 when Opus 5 at higher effort still falls short. Now the Claude Code default Fable model (v2.1.257); not on Priority Tier; 30-day retention required. What it means: if you pin claude-fable-5, grep for forced tool_choice and for any code that edits conversation history before flipping the ID. Full migration guide with the seven documented behavior shifts (fewer parallel tool calls, less narration, whole-file rewrites) and Anthropic's launch benchmark table: Claude Fable 5.1: What Changed and How to Migrate. Last verified: 2026-09-14. IDs, pricing, breaking changes, and beta headers from Anthropic's "What's new in Claude Fable 5.1" and the models overview; retirement not sooner than September 1, 2027. Benchmarks from the launch announcement. Run /claude-api migrate this project to claude-fable-5-1 in Claude Code to automate the ID swap and parameter fixes. Confirm against the official source. 🧠 Models (cross-AI) — OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra (gpt-6-astra) went GA on September 4, 2026 after a September 3 limited release, ending the five-week "preview with no price" period. Confirmed specs: 1,050,000-token context (922K max input), 128K output, April 30, 2026 cutoff, $10 / $50 per MTok, cached input $1.00, Chat Completions + Responses + Batch (tools need Responses; no Realtime, Assistants, or fine-tuning), reasoning effort low through max, and the GPT-5.6-style 272K cliff (cross it and the whole request is re-priced 2× input / 1.5× output). Independent numbers from Artificial Analysis (September 9): tied with Claude Fable 5.1 at 53 on the Intelligence Index and 62 on the Coding Agent Index, at roughly a third of the output tokens and 40% less cost per task; ahead on Terminal-Bench 4.0 (59% vs 52%); behind GPT-5.6 Sol on GDPval-AA v2. Safety: first OpenAI model at the Critical cyber tier, exploit capability gated behind a vetted-access program, and a system card that says chain-of-thought monitorability decreased versus Sol because the "recurrent depth" architecture moves reasoning inside the model. What it means: Astra and Fable 5.1 are now peers on agentic coding at the same list price, but the bills diverge on long loops (Astra's cache reads are 4× Fable 5.1's) and the benchmarks were run at max effort while the API defaults lower. Full comparison, the four API gotchas, and a per-workload decision table: GPT-6 Astra: The Field Guide for Claude Users. Last verified: 2026-09-14. Specs and pricing from OpenAI's developer model page; safety facts from the GPT-6 Astra system card; benchmarks from Artificial Analysis. OpenAI did not publish a SWE-bench Verified score for Astra. Confirm against the official source. 🛠️ Claude Code — The first two weeks of September (v2.1.257–v2.1.270) shipped a run of practical tooling. /skill-doctor (v2.1.252+, September 4) reports what each loaded skill costs in context per turn, how often it's invoked, and flags never-used skills with instructions for where to turn them off; prune the highest-cost unused ones first (not available over Remote Control). claude plugin eval <plugin> (v2.1.268+, September 11) runs a plugin's eval suite, JSON cases in evals/ or the experimental.evals manifest field, and produces scored, reproducible JSON + HTML reports; claude plugin validate --json --strict turns warnings into CI failures. /diff (v2.1.260) opens a side-by-side panel of uncommitted changes as Claude edits in fullscreen mode. /cost and the status line's prompt_cache field now name the likely cause of a cache miss (tool definitions or system prompt changed, idle past the TTL). For fleets: maxEffortLevel (v2.1.267) caps effort per model on every provider; --permission-prompts none (v2.1.259) auto-denies anything that would prompt on unattended headless hosts; managedMcpServers lets an org push HTTP/SSE MCP servers to every user; bashEditDiffEnabled appends a diff of files a Bash command changed to the tool result; CLAUDE_CODE_WORKFLOW_MAX_CONCURRENT_AGENTS (1–256) raises the Workflow tool's fan-out cap; /output-style [name] now works in headless and Remote Control sessions. What it means: /skill-doctor is the fastest context-budget win available today; run it once per project and delete what it flags. The plugin eval command is the first native way to regression-test a plugin before publishing. Last verified: 2026-09-14. Claude Code changelog entries dated September 1–12, 2026. /skill-doctor reference in the skills docs; claude plugin eval and experimental.evals in the plugins reference. v2.1.257 also made Claude Fable 5.1 the default Fable model with the $0.25 cache-read rate reflected in /cost. Confirm against the official source. 🛠️ Claude Code — A fifth built-in output style, Concise, shipped in v2.1.237 (Week 34, Aug 17–21 2026) — Claude leads with the result, skips preamble and narration, and keeps responses short by default, while doing the engineering work as thoroughly as Default. Ask for detail and it answers in full; error reports, security warnings, and destructive-action confirmations stay complete regardless — Concise never quiets the things you must not miss. Same window also landed force-for-plugin in output-style frontmatter (a plugin can auto-apply its style and override the user's outputStyle setting — use sparingly), and made nested project-level styles resolve closest-directory-wins so a package inside a monorepo can override the workspace default. Styles still don't cross into subagents (each subagent runs its own system prompt), but /fork is the one exception — it copies the parent's full prompt and therefore keeps the style. What it means: if you kept re-prompting for "just the result, no preamble" every session, drop the ceremony and set "outputStyle": "Concise" in ~/.claude/settings.json. Full rewrite with the five-style comparison table, subagent-scope rules, the frontmatter field reference, and a quiz covering all of it: Output Styles. Last verified: 2026-08-31. Concise requires Claude Code v2.1.237 or later. Frontmatter field force-for-plugin is plugin-only; when multiple enabled plugins set it, Claude Code uses the first one loaded. Project styles load from every .claude/output-styles/ between the working directory and the repo root; when two levels define the same name, the closest directory to the working directory wins. Confirm against the official source. 🔌 API — Anthropic made Claude Sonnet 5's introductory pricing permanent on August 10–11, 2026 — the $2 / $10 per MTok launch price was scheduled to jump to $3 / $15 on September 1, and that increase will not happen. Same model ID (claude-sonnet-5), same 1M context, same 128k output — just no price hike. What it means: budgets, evals, and cost forecasts you built assuming a September price jump can stand down. If you deferred a Sonnet-5 migration because of the impending increase, there's no longer a September cliff to plan around. The Current Models & Pricing page keeps pointing to Anthropic's official pricing page as authoritative — a stale price on our site is worse than none. Last verified: 2026-08-31. Announcement by @claudeai (Aug 10–11, 2026): "We're making Claude Sonnet 5's introductory pricing permanent. We launched Sonnet 5 in June at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens through August 31, and that price will remain unchanged." Cross-verified in the Anthropic pricing page and the Anthropic Claude Developer Platform release notes. Confirm against the official source. 🔌 API (cross-AI) — Cloudflare shipped Kitesurf on August 6, 2026 — a stateless, agent-first browser runtime that runs entirely in V8 isolates on Workers, discarding the Chromium engine that has underpinned nearly every headless browser tool for the past decade. Cloudflare's own benchmarks: 3.1× less CPU and 4.7× less memory than Chromium on screenshots, 3.8× less CPU and 7.0× less memory on HTML extraction — traded for about 1.7–1.8× more wall-clock time per task (Boa interprets JS instead of V8-JIT-ing it). Kitesurf speaks the Chrome DevTools Protocol, so Puppeteer, Playwright, chrome-remote-interface, and chrome-devtools-mcp connect unchanged via a single --wsEndpoint swap. Rendering uses Firefox's CSS engine (Stylo) and the Rust Blitz engine — that's how a 12-week-old project already passes 235,000+ Web Platform Test subtests. Free public beta today; open-source release planned. Four things it cannot do yet: video, WebGL, TLS-fingerprint bot-challenge negotiation, persistent authenticated sessions. What it means: the browser stack for agents and the browser stack for humans are diverging into two products. If you run any bursty, short, HTML-shaped browsing workload on per-CPU-second billing, Kitesurf changes the math — see the full practical read at Cloudflare Kitesurf: The First Browser Runtime Built for AI Agents. Last verified: 2026-08-24. Cloudflare launch post (Aug 6, 2026); official docs at Kitesurf on Browser Run. Benchmark methodology and the 235,000+ WPT subtest count are Cloudflare's; per-account beta limits apply. Confirm against the official source. 🛠️ Claude Code — Auto mode becomes the default permission mode on August 14, 2026 for new sessions on Pro, Max, and Team plans (Week 32 digest, v2.1.220–v2.1.224). Instead of stopping to ask on every non-read action, Claude Code proceeds unless a separate classifier judges the action irreversible, destructive, or aimed outside your environment (curl | bash, force pushes, prod deploys, rm -rf on unresolved variables, transcript tampering, destructive git that discards uncommitted work, secret exfiltration). Anthropic's own justification: in a study of over 1,000 paid users, the auto-mode classifier caught 89% of harmful actions vs 13.6% for manual review — because habituated users approved about 97% of prompts without reading them.
